findings.title: members (io not delegated) recorded two Io(ENOENT) collection errors on every snapshot
findings.change: Snapshot.read_bytes/write_bytes: Result<IoBytes, Failure>, IoBytes::{Counted(u64), NotDelegated}; NotDelegated is omitted from shards.cgroup.disk.io and not counted in shards.cgroup.collection.error.count. The reader consults the cgroup's own cgroup.controllers only after io.stat fails ENOENT; a listing without io gives NotDelegated; a listing with io, an unreadable listing, or any other failure keeps the failure. Delegated controllers unchanged.
sources: Linux v6.18 Documentation/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.rst 484-489 (enabling a controller creates its interface files in the children) and 935-940 (cgroup.controllers)
crates/init/src/run.rs cgroups(): root and run enable +io one at a time, a missing controller stays off
findings.live_premise: runs/cgroup-io-probe.log: io.stat present exactly where cgroup.controllers lists io in 1150 of 1150 live cgroups (983 listed+present, 167 unlisted+absent)
alternatives: static per-scope rule (Member => not delegated): rejected, it copies admission's delegation into metrics as a hidden cross-module obligation (R05/R06) and would silently drop io if members were ever given it
read cgroup.controllers for every scope before io.stat: rejected, extra syscalls on run and workload scopes where io.stat exists
chosen: read the kernel's listing only after ENOENT (authoritative, no cache, no cost where io.stat exists)

red.key_output: member OTLP shards.cgroup.collection.error.count asInt "2" (disk.io read and write, error.type io, errno 2); left: "2" right: "0"

mutation.removed: only the arm Err(Failure::Io(ENOENT)) if self.enabled(group, b"io") == Ok(false) => NotDelegated

findings.title: engine relay logged a client's normal departure as a fault
findings.change: relay() passes its post-HELLO part to forward(conn, host, slots, log), which reads the pump's typed result as End::{Ended, ClientDeparted, Fault(Fault)} and says only Fault. ClientDeparted = client leg, Read with ECONNRESET, or Write with EPIPE or ECONNRESET. relay.rs (shared pump), buffer size and threading unchanged.
sources: Linux v6.18 net/unix/af_unix.c 696-711 (a closing peer sets the relay socket's shutdown both ways, and sk_err ECONNRESET if it left bytes unread)
af_unix.c 2995 (unix_stream_read_generic: sock_error before EOF gives ECONNRESET)
Linux v6.18 net/core/sock.c 2945-2947 (sock_alloc_send_pskb returns sock_error first: a write racing the close can see ECONNRESET)
the pre-pump relay ignored copy errors (git show 1be384ecb -- crates/init/src/engine.rs)
alternatives: Termination::ClientDeparted inside the pump: rejected, relay.rs is path-shared with testguest's TCP fixture, where a client-leg ECONNRESET is a fault it acts on (reset_peer), and ROOT's carried evidence pins the pump's hash
chosen: the engine caller's typed reading of the pump's result (relay.rs: terminal policy comes from the caller)
findings.seam: patches/f3-seam-only.patch: behavior-preserving extraction of forward(conn, host, slots, log); relay passes io::stderr()

findings.title: optional: admission has_word one byte per read(2), enable() reopens files, Committed opens cgroup.kill/cgroup.events again opened by Launch::new
verified_in_source: domains/admission.rs has_word reads one byte per read; enable() opens cgroup.controllers twice and cgroup.subtree_control up to four times to read (once more to write where a controller is missing); it runs twice per Parent::prepare (run and domains), once per domains start (domains.rs 1380)

Prepared::commit opens cgroup.kill and cgroup.events as _kill/_events, never used, dropped by into_file after clone3; managed.rs Launch::new (265-266) opens both again, once per member (domains.rs 1617-1618, 1779)
why_deferred: no strace on the runner (runs/env-probe.log), so no strace -c before/after

a buffered has_word needs a production buffer bound derived under R03 (candidate: at most 16 subsystems, v6.18 kernel/cgroup/cgroup.c 6354, of at most 32-byte names, include/linux/cgroup-defs.h 37) and a read-count seam: a design change beyond a light fix

dropping Committed's opens moves a documented reservation ('Reserve the existing lifecycle controls before the first release') and its typed Refusal/rollback point into managed::Launch, an ownership/API decision for ROOT (R02/R05)
the costs are on the domain start path, whose profiling ROOT owns
